column1: # Listed bodies whose own control flow reaches past functions.tsv's body_bytes.
# METHOD: from each listed entry, walk the control-flow graph over [entry, next listed entry)
# following direct branches and RESOLVING image-base-relative jump tables - MSVC emits
# `mov ecx, dword ptr [r12 + rax*4 + disp]` / `add rcx, r12` / `jmp rcx` with r12 the image
# base, so the table is at BASE + disp and its entries are RVAs. A body is listed here when
# the END of its last reachable NON-PADDING instruction exceeds entry + body_bytes.
# PADDING IS NOT A TRUNCATION: counting the terminating int3 gave 592 rows, 394 of them
# overshooting by zero bytes. That figure was two thirds artefact and is not reported.
# CONTROL: 0037C3F0, FABLE's case - recorded 248 bytes, eleven arms resolved, nine past the
# recorded end, code reaching 0037C6F8. A run that does not reproduce it reports nothing.
# THIS IS NOT THE SAME SET AS FABLE's 457. That was the SIGNATURE population - an indirect
# jmp in the recorded body plus more than 16 bytes of unlisted space - which FABLE stated is
# suggestive rather than proof per case. This is the resolved measurement: 177 bodies.
